user_message: A friend told me a company growing 50%/year is necessarily a great investment. Push back?
assistant_message: Revenue growth is *neither necessary nor sufficient* for shareholder value creation. It can be value-destructive when the marginal investment required to fund the growth earns below the cost of capital. The reusable mental model is: separate the growth rate from the economics of the marginal dollar. A company with 5% revenue growth but 80% incremental ROIC creates more shareholder value than a 50% grower with 3% incremental ROIC. Don't pay a growth multiple — pay an economics multiple.
